subject: HealthCore — SLA measurement methodology & crediting clarifications
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@healthcore.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: SLA measurement methodology + crediting (RFP)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this RFP — we include a detailed SLA questionnaire as part of our procurement packet. Attached is HealthCore_SLA_Template.docx with the sections we need filled: availability definition, measurement windows, telemetry sources, and the service credit calculation formula.

A few specific asks up front so we can slot this into legal:
- How do you define availability at the endpoint level vs. regional routing?
- What probes/telemetry do you use to measure availability and latency (synthetic probes, customer request sampling, platform telemetry)?
- Provide a concrete example calculation for service credits for a 30-day billing month when the target is 99.95% uptime and observed uptime is 99.80%.
- How are partial degradations (e.g., 20% traffic impacted for 12 hours) attributed to credits?
- What is your dispute resolution workflow / evidence exchange window?

If you can return a short written response plus any attachments with sample calculations by EOD Monday (2028-06-13), that would help our legal review. Also let us know if you prefer a 30-minute call to walk through.

Attachments: HealthCore_SLA_Template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Regards,
Dana Li
Sourcing Manager — HealthCore
procurement@healthcore.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@healthcore.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-11T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA measurement methodology + crediting (RFP)

Hi Dana — thanks for the template and the clear asks. Below is a concise response to each item plus attachments with worked examples. If helpful we can review live; I'm available Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Summary (high level)
- Measurement sources: availability is computed from a weighted blend of synthetic probes (external vantage points) and production telemetry (successful token-generation and HTTP 2xx/3xx responses). Probe weight defaults to 60% production telemetry / 40% synthetic, but is configurable per contract.
- Boundaries & aggregation: availability is measured per-region and per-route; monthly availability is a weighted average across region windows using traffic-based normalization.
- Partial degradation: credits are computed pro-rata by impacted traffic and time. Example provided below.
- Credit formula: we compute percentage shortfall against the monthly target and apply the credit matrix (see attachment). Dispute window: 14 business days to exchange evidence, 30 business days resolution target.

Key details
- Availability definition: percentage of successful requests over total measured requests for a given route and region, where success = response within agreed latency bound and HTTP semantics OK (200/202/204).
- Measurement cadence: production telemetry sampled at per-request resolution with 99% of requests represented; synthetic probes run every 30s from 6 vantage regions with jitter to avoid synchronization.
- Windowing: we use rolling 1-minute windows aggregated into hourly buckets, then compute monthly availability from hourly aggregates. Burst windows (short transient spikes) are attenuated using a 5-minute smoothing kernel for metrics used solely for operator alerts, but credits are computed from raw hourly aggregates.
- Regional weighting: weights are proportional to observed customer traffic in the billing month (example in attachment). If traffic data is not available, we default to equal regional weighting across active regions.

Service credit example (summary)
- Contract SLA: 99.95% monthly availability
- Observed availability (global weighted): 99.80%
- Monthly allowed downtime at 99.95% = ~21.6 minutes in a 30-day month
- Observed downtime equivalent = ~43.2 minutes
- Shortfall = 21.6 minutes → translate to percentage shortfall = (99.95 - 99.80) = 0.15%
- Credit: per our standard matrix, 0.10%–0.25% shortfall = 10% monthly credit. See slo-examples-calc.xlsx for line-by-line math.

Attachments included: redwood-slo-measurement-appendix.pdf (PDF), slo-examples-calc.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps
- I can share a redacted sample of probe logs and an example CSV of hourly aggregates after we sign a narrow NDA; quick call to align would speed things up.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Dana Li <dana.li@healthcore.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthcore.com
Date: 2028-06-12T08:50:20-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA measurement methodology + crediting (RFP)

Mateo — thanks, that is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions to ensure our legal and SRE teams can map this into our template: 

1) Regional weighting: can you provide the exact formula you use to convert per-region traffic into weights? We want reproducibility in the contract (e.g., "weight_i = traffic_i / sum(traffic_all_active) over the billing month").
2) Partial degradation math: your note about pro-rata by impacted traffic — can you show a short numeric example where 20% of traffic is impacted for 12 hours?
3) Are synthetic probes included in the numerator/denominator or only used to supplement detection? If they are used, do you de-duplicate probe signals vs. production telemetry?
4) For dispute resolution, what artifacts will you provide? We need: hourly aggregates csv, raw probe logs (sample), and a short description of the aggregation pipeline.

If you can return those items and the numeric worked example by EOD Monday, that should keep us on the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Dana

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-12T17:30:45-07:00

Mateo/Laura — forwarding Dana's follow-ups. Suggested items to include in our written reply (keep contract-friendly language):

- Regional weighting formula: "weight_i = traffic_i / sum(traffic_all_active) where traffic_i is sum of successful requests in region i during the billing month as observed by Redwood's production telemetry. If customer provides server-side traffic numbers, those will be used when mutually agreed in writing."

- Partial degradation example (draft language): "If only a subset of customer traffic is impacted in a region, Redwood will compute the credit pro-rata by impacted traffic: Credit_shortfall = (target_availability - observed_availability) * (impacted_traffic_fraction). Example calculation provided in appendix."

- Synthetic probes: include as a secondary signal; probes are de-duplicated and used for early detection. Contract must state which signals are authoritative — recommend production telemetry as authoritative except where telemetry is unavailable, in which case synthetic probes are used as a fallback.

- Evidence artifacts: we will provide hourly_aggregates.csv, a redacted redwood-probe-sample.log, and a short "aggregation_pipeline.md" that explains how hourly numbers are computed from raw events. Allow 14 business days for evidence review; escalate to designated contacts if unresolved.

Recommend we prepare the appendix with the numeric example and the CSV/trace samples. Laura, can you review the legal phrasing? Mateo, I'll draft the appendix and attach the example calc file.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@healthcore.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-13T10:05:12-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA measurement methodology + crediting (RFP)

Dana — thanks for the follow-up. Below are the specific formulas and a worked numeric example per your request. I attached the CSV and probe sample to make it concrete.

1) Regional weighting (formal)
weight_i = traffic_i / sum(traffic_all_active)
where traffic_i = sum(successful_requests_i) for region i over the billing month as observed in Redwood production telemetry. If customer supplies mutually-agreed traffic counters, those may be used by written amendment.

2) Partial degradation example (numeric)
- Scenario: 30-day month; contract target = 99.95%
- Total traffic = 1,000,000 requests in month
- Region A traffic = 400,000; Region B = 300,000; Region C = 300,000
- Impact: Region B has a degraded edge that affects 20% of Region B traffic for 12 hours.

Calculation steps:
A) Impacted requests = RegionB_traffic * impacted_fraction * (hours_impacted / (24*days)) = 300,000 * 0.20 * (12 / (24*30)) = 300,000 * 0.20 * 0.0166667 ≈ 1,000 requests impacted equivalent.
B) Convert impacted requests to downtime equivalent (using average request rate): In this model we map request failures to equivalent downtime by comparing against total expected request rate; for the worked sheet, see slo-examples-calc.xlsx.
C) Example result: the event produces an effective global availability drop from 99.95% to 99.92% (illustrative). Shortfall = 0.03% → per contract matrix that maps to a 5% monthly credit. Exact numeric mapping is in the attached spreadsheet.

3) Synthetic probes
- Probes are included as an advisory signal; production telemetry (per-request success/fail) is the authoritative source for credit calculations. We deduplicate probe events where the probe targets the same endpoint and timestamp as a measured production request.

4) Evidence artifacts provided on request (redacted)
- hourly_aggregates.csv (columns: timestamp, region, route, total_requests, successful_requests, availability_pct)
- redwood-probe-sample.log (redacted sample showing probe timestamp, vantage, latency_ms, status)
- aggregation_pipeline.md (short doc describing sampling and aggregation rules)

Attachments included with this email: slo-examples-calc.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet); redwood-probe-sample.log (text/plain); redwood-slo-measurement-appendix.pdf (application/pdf)

Drive: https://drive.google.com/redwood/HC-2028-0042/slo-appendix (redacted artifacts)

Proposed next steps
- We can provide the redacted artifacts under a narrow NDA if needed.
- If the numeric examples above look good, legal can accept the appendix language and we can slot this for a final review call next week.

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet on a call — I can demo the aggregation and the sample logs for your SRE team.

Best regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
